$comment: #VAPP-282 (round 7): THE month grid of a DatePicker, the same in its popup and `inline: true` (the calendar applet). Six weeks of seven `day` cells, ids `<id>.day.<row>.<col>`, starting on `firstDayOfWeek` (else the locale's week start); `leading` days of the previous month, then the month, then `trailing` days of the next (always 42 cells; leading + trailing days carry `outside`). The view opens on `value`'s month, else `today`'s (the prop, else the host's today), else `min`'s. The `previous` / `next` steppers move the view one month (across years) and fire `month {month: yyyy-mm}` (never `change`). `today` rings that day (recipe prop `today`), `value` selects it (state `selected`), `outside` dims (recipe prop `outside`). `marks` [{date, tone}] put ONE event dot on each listed day of the grid (outside days too; a later mark on the same day is ignored; no tone = primary): `mark` on the day = the tone. Replayed by the TS reference (`monthView` in src/web/dates.ts, which the React and Solid grids paint) and the Rust core (`eui-core/tests/month_grid.rs` over the laid-out inline DatePicker, whose `day` nodes SwiftUI, Compose and gpui paint). `first`/`last` = the first and last cell's date; positions are `row.col`.

cases.name: October 2026, Sunday first: four leading, seven trailing
October 2026, Monday first: three leading, eight trailing
February 2026 starts on the week start: no leading, fourteen trailing
no value: the view opens on today's month (Saturday first)
next across the year end fires month, keeps the value
previous twice from January 2026 lands on November 2025
